correctness.rationale: The Moore bound and girth identities imply the two-pair adjacency table for all \(d\ge2\). A permanent two/three-pebble strategy follows from positive pattern supports; degree two lacks precisely one nonedge-pair pattern, witnessed by an independent triple. The four-variable sentence binds only x,y,z,w and the centered triple anti-neighbor count \(d(d-3)\) follows from unique pairwise common neighbors. Each quantifier and boundary case has been reconstructed; exact code checks give C5 (n5,d2), Petersen (n10,d3), Hoffman–Singleton (n50,d7). No finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result exactly classifies unrestricted \(\mathrm{FO}^{3}\) theories across all possible diameter-two Moore valencies and all \(\mathrm{FO}^{2}\) theories, obtains the sharp minimum distinguishing width for every pair among all three existing graphs, and exploits a geometric three-point obstruction to give a four-variable separation that is not supplied by merely writing a degree-at-least-four formula (which needs five names). The contrast with \(\mathrm{C}^{2}\) neighbor counting makes this a motivated expressivity boundary for a canonical extremal family, not an arbitrary finite-table fact.
